title: InputSourcesBar uses non-unique varName as React key, causing key collisions and mis-targeted delete buttons when two upstream sources share a sanitized name
description: InputSourcesBar renders `inputSources.map((src) => <span key={src.varName} ...>)`. `varName` is NOT unique: in NodePanel.tsx (line 636) it is computed as `sanitizeName(nodeMap[e.source]?.data.label || e.source)`, derived from the upstream node label. sanitizeName is many-to-one, so distinct upstream nodes whose labels collapse to the same identifier produce identical `varName` values and therefore duplicate React keys. The struct already carries a guaranteed-unique `edgeId` (e.g. used as the delete payload `onDeleteInput(src.edgeId)`), which is the correct key.
evidence: Producer (NodePanel.tsx lines 632-639): `upstreamEdges.map((e) => ({ sourceNodeId: e.source, varName: sanitizeName(nodeMap[e.source]?.data.label || e.source), sourceLabel: ..., edgeId: e.id }))`. sanitizeName (utils/sanitizeName.ts:18-19) replaces `[\s-]` with `_` and strips non-alnum/underscore, so labels like `"Age Band"`, `"Age-Band"`, `"Age_Band"`, and `"Age Band!"` all sanitize to `"Age_Band"`. Two upstream nodes with such labels yield two inputSources entries with identical `varName` -> `key={src.varName}` collides. React then logs a duplicate-key warning and, on reconciliation, can associate the click handler / DOM of the wrong entry; clicking one delete-X may remove the other source's edge (both call onDeleteInput but the reconciled element identity is ambiguous). Fix: `key={src.edgeId}` (edgeId = e.id, unique per edge).
